about: Email rules UMS checks drafts against, and the sequences it scaffolds. Rules marked practice are working thresholds, not platform limits; see references/email.md for sources.

notes.subjectWarnAt: practice: phone inboxes show roughly the first 30-50 characters
notes.clipBytes: Gmail clips messages larger than about 102 KB

welcome.name: Welcome
welcome.why: The emails people open most are the first ones after they sign up; use them to deliver what was promised and ask for one action.

emails.subject: what they signed up for, delivered
emails.job: deliver exactly what the signup promised for {name}, say what comes next and how often
emails.cta: the one thing to do first

emails.subject: why {name} exists, in one line
emails.job: the founder in their own voice: the problem that started {name}, one real detail
emails.cta: reply with what they are trying to do

emails.subject: a result someone got
emails.job: one real result with permission, or a short how-to that gets the reader the same result

onboarding.name: Onboarding and trial
onboarding.why: Activation, not information: each email moves a new user one step toward the moment the product proves itself.

emails.subject: the first step, in one sentence
emails.job: the single action that gets a new {name} user to the first result

emails.when: day 1, only if the first step is not done
emails.subject: the most common place people get stuck
emails.job: the snag most new users hit and how to get past it

emails.subject: the second thing worth doing
emails.job: the feature that makes {name} stick, shown in one example

emails.subject: trial ends on a date, plainly
emails.job: what they keep, what stops, the price, and how to cancel

launch.name: Launch
launch.why: A list that hears first converts first; three to four emails around the date, each with one job.

emails.subject: the date and what is launching
emails.job: what {name} is launching, the date, and the one reason it matters to this reader
emails.cta: add it to the calendar or wishlist

emails.subject: tomorrow
emails.job: a short reminder with one new detail (a clip, a price, a time)

emails.subject: it is live
emails.job: it is out, where to get it, the launch offer if there is one and when it really ends

emails.when: 2 days after, only if there is a real deadline
emails.subject: the real deadline
emails.job: the actual end of a real offer; skip this email if there is none

game-launch.name: Game launch (Steam)
game-launch.why: Wishlists notify on launch, but your own list is the one channel you control.

emails.subject: the demo is playable
emails.job: the demo for {name} is live during the festival; one clip, how long it takes to play

emails.subject: release date
emails.job: the release date, price and launch discount if any

emails.subject: it is out
emails.job: {name} is out; the launch discount and its real end date

winback.name: Win-back and sunset
winback.why: Quiet subscribers hurt deliverability; ask once or twice, then remove the ones who stay quiet.

emails.subject: still want these
emails.job: ask plainly whether they still want emails from {name}, with what they will get

emails.subject: the best thing we sent
emails.job: one genuinely useful thing from the archive

emails.subject: removing you, unless
emails.job: say they will be removed in a few days unless they click; then remove them (sunset)
